mainTopic: The four אבות נזיקין, and how אבות and תולדות relate in נזיקין, שבת, and טומאה.
overview: This amud opens מסכת בבא קמא with a משנה listing the four אבות נזיקין: שור, בור, מבעה, and הבער. The משנה shows that each has a feature the others lack, so no one category could be learned from another. It then names what all four share: damage is normal for them, and you must guard them. When they cause damage, the one responsible pays with מיטב הארץ. The גמרא notes that the word אבות implies there are תולדות. It asks whether those תולדות follow the same law as their אבות. To explore this, it looks at שבת. There a תולדה brings the same חטאת and סקילה as its אב, and the labels matter only for counting how many חטאות are owed. For רבי אליעזר, the names only reflect whether a labor was important in the משכן. The גמרא then begins quoting the משנה that lists the אבות of טומאה, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The four main categories of damage
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens the מסכתא by listing the four אבות נזיקין: שור, בור, מבעה, and הבער.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are four main categories of damage: the Ox, the Pit, the מבעה, and Fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the four main types of damage that a person can be held responsible for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An 'אב' (literally 'father') is a main category, and smaller cases will later be grouped under it. The meaning of מבעה is not clear from the משנה itself. The גמרא will later discuss whether it means an animal's tooth (eating) or a person who causes damage.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
The main categories of damage
Ox; damage done by an animal
Pit; an obstacle someone leaves that others fall into
A category whose meaning the גמרא debates: an animal's tooth or a person
Fire; damage from a fire someone started

phrases.english: MISHNA: There are four primary categories of damage:
the Ox, and the Pit,
and the Maveh, and the Fire.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four main categories of damage: שור, בור, מבעה, הבער.

steps.title: Ox and Maveh differ, and both differ from Fire
steps.stepSummary: The משנה shows that שור and מבעה are each unique, and that both of them, as living things, are different from fire, which is not alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Ox is not like the מבעה, and the מבעה is not like the Ox. Both of these are alive, so they are not like Fire, which is not alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins showing that each category is unique, so we could not have learned one from another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First it says שור and מבעה each have something special, without saying what it is yet. Then it adds a clear difference: both are living things (רוח חיים), while fire is not. So you cannot learn the laws of fire from the two living categories.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The nature of this is not like the nature of that'; a way of showing two things are different
A living spirit; being a living, moving creature
Fire; the same category the list called הבער

steps.confusionAlert: The list called the fourth category הבער, but here the משנה calls it אש. They are the same category: Fire.

phrases.english: The nature of the Ox is not like the nature of the Maveh,
and the nature of the Maveh is not like the nature of the Ox;

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא זֶה וָזֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן רוּחַ חַיִּים,
phrases.english: and neither this one nor that one, which have a living spirit,
phrases.notes: 'This one and that one' here means the Ox and the מבעה.

phrases.aramaic: כַּהֲרֵי הָאֵשׁ שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים;
phrases.english: is like Fire, which has no living spirit;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining why each listed category is needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שור and מבעה are each unique, and living damagers cannot teach us about fire, which is not alive.

steps.title: The moving damagers differ from the Pit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that the three categories that move and cause damage are different from a pit, which stays in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Ox, the מבעה, and Fire all normally move along and cause damage. They are not like the Pit, which does not move along to cause damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shows how the Pit is different from all the other categories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ox, מבעה, and Fire all travel to the thing they damage. A pit stays still, and the victim comes to it. Because of this difference, the laws of a pit could not be learned from the others.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one; here, Ox and מבעה together with Fire
Their normal way is to move along and cause damage

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא זֶה וָזֶה שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לֵילֵךְ וּלְהַזִּיק,
phrases.english: and neither this one nor that one, whose way is to move along and cause damage,
phrases.notes: Now 'this one' means Ox and מבעה, and 'that one' means Fire.

phrases.english: is like the Pit,
whose way is not to move along and cause damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא זֶה וָזֶה שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לֵילֵךְ וּלְהַזִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of differences, now separating the Pit
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pit stays in place, unlike the moving damagers, so its laws cannot be learned from them.

steps.title: What all four share, and the obligation to pay
steps.stepSummary: The משנה names the shared features of all four categories and states that the owner must pay for damage with the best quality property.
steps.simpleTranslation: What all of them have in common: they normally cause damage, and you are responsible for guarding them. When one of them causes damage, the one responsible must pay for the damage with the best of his land.
steps.whatsHappening: After showing how the categories differ, the משנה now shows what they all have in common and gives the law that applies to all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared features are: (1) damage is normal for them, and (2) the owner must guard them. When one of them causes damage, the one responsible must pay for the damage (תשלומי נזק), and he pays with his best quality property (מיטב הארץ).

keyTerms.meaning: The common side; the feature all cases share
Guarding them is your responsibility
The one who caused the damage, or the owner responsible for it
Payment for damage
The best of the land; paying with top quality property

steps.whatToRemember: Four אבות נזיקין: שור, בור, מבעה, הבער. Each has something unique, so none can be learned from another. All share two things: damage is normal for them, and you must guard them. When they cause damage, the owner pays with מיטב הארץ.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of הצד השוה, finding what different cases share, becomes a key tool in the גמרא for applying these laws to other kinds of damage.

phrases.english: The common feature among them
is that their way is to cause damage,
and guarding them is your responsibility;
and when it caused damage,
the one responsible for the damage is obligated to pay for the damage,
with the best of the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the differences to the shared features and the final law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All four normally cause damage and must be guarded, and the owner pays with the best quality property.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Despite their differences, all four אבות נזיקין share being normal damagers that require guarding, and when they cause damage the one responsible pays with מיטב הארץ.

steps.title: If there are primary categories, are their subcategories treated the same?
steps.stepSummary: From the word אבות in the משנה, the גמרא infers that תולדות exist. It then asks whether those תולדות share the same laws as their אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה says "primary categories," so there must also be subcategories. Are the subcategories like the primary ones, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by reading closely the word אבות in the משנה. It asks a basic question: do the 'offspring' categories follow the same rules as the 'parent' categories?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling something a 'father' suggests it has 'children,' so the word אבות tells us תולדות exist. What the word does not tell us is whether a תולדה is punished or paid for exactly like its אב. That open question drives the rest of this section.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the חכמים that explains the משנה
'Fathers': the main, primary categories
'Offspring': subcategories that come out of a main category
By inference; it can be understood from
Like them; following the same laws

phrases.english: GEMARA
From the fact that it teaches "primary categories"
by inference, there are subcategories;
are their subcategories like them,
or not like them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by reading closely the word אבות from the משנה's list in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the תולדות of the damage categories have the same laws as their אבות.

steps.title: Bringing in the example of שבת, which also has primary categories
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in שבת that lists 39 אבות מלאכות. It notes that there, too, the word אבות implies תולדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: About שבת we learned: the primary categories of labor are forty minus one. Since it says "primary categories," there must also be subcategories.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא brings a parallel case from שבת, which also uses the word אבות, so it can see how that area treats אבות and תולדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same reasoning used on our משנה is applied to the משנה in שבת: the word אבות means there are תולדות. This prepares the next step, which explains how שבת's תולדות are treated.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding; in the area of
The main categories of work forbidden on שבת
Forty minus one, which is 39

phrases.english: Regarding שבת we learned:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in שבת 73a.

phrases.english: The primary categories of labor are forty minus one.
"Primary categories": by inference, there are subcategories,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel area of halacha to start working out the question asked in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 39 מלאכות of שבת are called אבות, so שבת also has תולדות.

steps.title: In שבת, subcategories carry the same punishment as primary categories
steps.stepSummary: For שבת, a תולדה is just like its אב. Done by mistake, both require a חטאת. Done on purpose, both bring סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their subcategories are like them. A primary category brings a sin-offering, and a subcategory brings a sin-offering. A primary category brings stoning, and a subcategory brings stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the rule for שבת: there is no difference in punishment between an אב and a תולדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who does a תולדה is treated just as seriously as someone who does an אב. If he did it by mistake he brings a חטאת, and if he did it on purpose he gets סקילה. So at least in שבת, the answer to step 5's question is 'yes, they are alike.'

keyTerms.meaning: It makes no difference
A sin-offering, brought for a mistaken (unknowing) sin
Stoning, the punishment for breaking שבת on purpose

steps.confusionAlert: This rule is about שבת only. The גמרא has not yet answered whether the תולדות of נזיקין follow their אבות. It is using שבת as a comparison.

phrases.english: their subcategories are like them;
no difference: a primary category brings a sin-offering,
and no difference: a subcategory brings a sin-offering;
no difference: a primary category brings stoning,
phrases.notes: The חטאת lines are about doing it by mistake. The סקילה lines are about doing it on purpose.

phrases.english: and no difference: a subcategory brings stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶן כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן; לָא שְׁנָא אָב – חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the שבת אבות and תולדות introduced in step 6 are treated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In שבת, a תולדה carries the same חטאת and סקילה as its אב.

steps.title: So what is the difference between a primary category and a subcategory?
steps.stepSummary: If both bring the same punishment, the גמרא asks what practical difference there is between an אב and a תולדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what difference is there between a primary category and a subcategory?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a natural follow-up. If they are punished the same, why call one an 'אב' and the other a 'תולדה' at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the punishments are identical, the different names seem pointless. The גמרא wants to find the real-life case where the label actually changes the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between

phrases.english: And what difference is there between a primary category and a subcategory?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 7: if the punishments are the same, why have two separate labels?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between an אב and a תולדה in שבת.

steps.title: The difference shows up when counting how many sin-offerings are owed
steps.stepSummary: Two different אבות, or תולדות of two different אבות, done together make a person bring a חטאת for each one. An אב together with its own תולדה makes him bring only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference: if he does two primary categories together, or two subcategories together, he is liable for each one. But if he does a primary category together with its own subcategory, he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 8. The labels matter when someone does several מלאכות in one stretch of not realizing, and we need to count how many קרבנות he owes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אב counts as its own separate sin, so two אבות mean two חטאות. A תולדה belongs to its אב's 'family,' so doing an אב along with its own תולדה counts as only one sin. The label decides how many offerings are owed, not how severe each act is.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical difference that comes out of it
Together; in one go
For each and every one

steps.whatToRemember: In שבת, an אב and its תולדה are punished the same. The only difference is counting: separate אבות mean separate חטאות, while an אב and its own תולדה count as one. Next, the גמרא checks this answer against רבי אליעזר's view (step 10), and then turns to טומאה (step 12).

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ, דְּאִילּוּ עָבֵיד שְׁתֵּי אָבוֹת בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: The practical difference: if he does two primary categories together,
phrases.notes: "Together" means during one stretch of time when he didn't realize what he was doing, which is why the punishment is a חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי שְׁתֵּי תוֹלָדוֹת בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי –
phrases.english: or alternatively two subcategories together,
phrases.notes: He means subcategories that belong to two different main categories.

phrases.english: he is liable for each and every one;
whereas if he does a primary category and its own subcategory,
he is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ, דְּאִילּוּ עָבֵיד שְׁתֵּי אָבוֹת בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is in counting חטאות. Separate אבות, or their תולדות, each require their own חטאת, while an אב with its own תולדה requires only one.

steps.title: Why call it אב and תולדה according to רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that even an אב done together with its own תולדה requires two חטאות. So for him, what is the point of calling one an אב and the other a תולדה?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, who makes a person liable for a תולדה even when he also did its אב, why is one called an אב and the other called a תולדה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from the last step by looking at רבי אליעזר's opinion. For him, that answer does not work, so the גמרא asks what the names mean for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, the difference between אב and תולדה was that an אב with its own תולדה brings only one חטאת. רבי אליעזר disagrees and requires a separate חטאת for each. So for him that difference is gone, and the names seem to have no meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Together with the אב (done in the same lapse of awareness)
Why?
Calls it / names it

steps.confusionAlert: The answer in step 9 follows the view that an אב with its own תולדה brings one חטאת. רבי אליעזר does not hold that, which is exactly why this question comes up.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Eliezer,
who makes one liable for a subcategory done together with its primary category,
why does one call this one a primary category,
and why does one call that one a subcategory?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דִּמְחַיֵּיב אַתּוֹלָדָה בִּמְקוֹם אָב אַמַּאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of step 9 against רבי אליעזר's view, where that answer does not apply.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the names אב and תולדה mean for שבת according to רבי אליעזר, since for him they do not differ in the number of חטאות.

steps.title: An אב was an important labor in the משכן
steps.stepSummary: A labor that was important in building the משכן is called an אב. A labor that was not important there is called a תולדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The labor that was done in the משכן and was important there is called an אב. The labor that was not important in the משכן is called a תולדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי אליעזר the names are not about the law. They describe where each labor comes from: whether it was an important labor in the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden labors of שבת are learned from the work done in building the משכן. So even if the punishment and the number of חטאות are the same, the name tells us which labors were important in the משכן (אבות) and which were not (תולדות).

keyTerms.meaning: The Tabernacle, whose building work is the source of the labors forbidden on שבת
Important, significant
That one

steps.whatToRemember: For שבת: according to the רבנן, an אב with its own תולדה brings one חטאת. According to רבי אליעזר, the names only tell us whether the labor was an important one in the משכן.

phrases.english: That labor which was in the Tabernacle, being significant,
one calls it a primary category;
that labor which was not significant in the Tabernacle,
one calls it a subcategory.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָךְ דַּהֲוָה בְּמִשְׁכָּן חֲשִׁיבָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ אָב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The names reflect whether the labor was important in the משכן, not a difference in law.

steps.title: The משנה that lists the אבות of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to another area where the word אבות appears: the laws of טומאה. It begins quoting the משנה in כלים that lists the main sources of impurity, starting with the שרץ and שכבת זרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: About impurities, we learned in a משנה: the main sources of impurity are the creeping creature and semen, and the list goes on.
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next topic. After שבת, the גמרא brings a third area that uses the word אבות, the laws of טומאה, and starts quoting that משנה. The quote continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same pattern from steps 5–7 is being repeated: find a place where אבות appears, which tells us that תולדות exist too. Once the quote is finished, the גמרא will say how the תולדות of טומאה compare to their אבות.

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds of ritual impurity
The main sources of ritual impurity
One of the eight creeping creatures listed in the תורה that make things impure
Semen, which is a source of impurity

phrases.english: With regard to impurities, we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This is the first משנה in כלים (1:1).

phrases.english: The primary categories of impurity are:
the creeping creature, and semen,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves שבת and brings a new area where אבות appears, following the same pattern as step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה in כלים lists the אבות הטומאות, beginning with שרץ and שכבת זרע.
